admit site home-b of f2a9c4e1-0b7d-4c3a-9e2f-5a6b7c8d9e01 as community on fake (ubuntu 24.04)

step 1: claim the host
step 2: create /etc/paisans
step 3: record what admit installs
step 4: skip the mesh until its conf exists

step 5: start community's manager after the mesh
  user: order user@1002.service after wg-quick@psns-f2a9 at boot, so a container that publishes on the mesh address finds it; a manager running now is not restarted, and takes it at its next start. Until the mesh's conf is written, wg-quick@psns-f2a9 is skipped
  write /etc/systemd/system/user@1002.service.d/paisans-mesh.conf mode 0644:
    | # Written by paisans site admit for deployment f2a9; paisans site evict
    | # removes it. The user's manager, its Docker daemon and its containers
    | # start after the mesh at boot.
    | [Unit]
    | Wants=wg-quick@psns-f2a9.service
    | After=wg-quick@psns-f2a9.service
  run:
    $ systemctl daemon-reload

step 6: delegate cgroups to users
  delegation: let every user's manager delegate cpu cpuset io memory pids, for compose's limits; written before community's manager first starts
  write /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf mode 0644:
    | # Written by paisans site admit. Shared by every admitted deployment;
    | # paisans site evict removes it with the last of them.
    | [Service]
    | Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids
  run:
    $ systemctl daemon-reload

step 7: write the egress table
step 8: install the egress unit
step 9: load the egress table

step 10: enable linger for community
  linger: run community's manager, its Docker daemon and its timers without a login, and at boot
  run:
    $ loginctl enable-linger community

step 11: start community's manager
  linger: start user@1002.service and wait for it, which does nothing to a manager already running
  run:
    $ systemctl start user@1002.service

step 12: load br_netfilter
step 13: load br_netfilter at boot

step 14: write community's daemon.json
  daemon: userland proxy off, address pools clear of the mesh; written as community
  run:
    $ runuser -u community -- env -i HOME='/home/community' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1002/docker.sock sh -c 'umask 077 && mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/docker" && cat > "$HOME/.config/docker/.daemon.json.paisans-tmp" && mv -f "$HOME/.config/docker/.daemon.json.paisans-tmp" "$HOME/.config/docker/daemon.json"'
  stdin:
    | {
    |   "userland-proxy": false,
    |   "default-address-pools": [
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.17.0.0/16",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.18.0.0/16",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.19.0.0/16",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.20.0.0/14",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.24.0.0/14",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "172.28.0.0/14",
    |       "size": 24
    |     },
    |     {
    |       "base": "192.168.0.0/16",
    |       "size": 24
    |     }
    |   ]
    | }

step 15: install community's rootless Docker
  daemon: dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install --force, as community, which starts the daemon reading its daemon.json; --force because a system daemon may run beside it
  run:
    $ runuser -u community -- env -i HOME='/home/community' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1002/docker.sock sh -c 'dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install --force'

step 16: create /srv/paisans
step 17: create /srv/paisans/f2a9
step 18: create /etc/wireguard
step 19: create /usr/local/libexec/paisans
step 20: install the WireGuard helper
step 21: install the helper's sudoers line
step 22: allow 2222/tcp
step 23: allow all inbound on psns-f2a9
step 24: load softdog
step 25: load softdog at boot

step 26: give the watchdog to community
  watchdog: /etc/udev/rules.d/60-paisans-f2a9-watchdog.rules makes /dev/watchdog and /dev/watchdog0 community's, owner and group, mode 600
  write /etc/udev/rules.d/60-paisans-f2a9-watchdog.rules mode 0644:
    | # Written by paisans site admit: the watchdog is community's, for its
    | # Patroni. One deployment per host holds it; paisans site evict removes this.
    | SUBSYSTEM=="watchdog|misc", KERNEL=="watchdog*", OWNER="community", GROUP="community", MODE="0600"
  run:
    $ udevadm control --reload && udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=watchdog --subsystem-match=misc

step 27: write the admission record
step 28: add the operators' keys

present: docker: Engine 29.9.1
present: package: docker-ce-rootless-extras installed
present: package: uidmap installed
present: package: nftables installed
present: package: wireguard-tools installed
present: package: git installed
present: apparmor: rootlesskit's profile is loaded
present: user: community exists, uid 1002, in no privileged group, and sudo grants it nothing beyond admit's helper
present: user: community holds 231072-296607 in /etc/subuid
present: user: community holds 231072-296607 in /etc/subgid
present: egress: the host's on-link IPv6 prefixes, dropped: 2001:db8:1::/64
present: br_netfilter: nf_tables, which the host's iptables uses, is loaded
present: daemon: /home (ext2/ext3) has 42.9 GB free
present: mesh: nothing on this host overlaps 10.44.0.0/24
present: firewall: ufw active, its default policy left to the owner
present: forwarding: not needed, this site has no endpoint
present: swap: on
warning: user: community already exists and is not paisans-f2a9
  admit adds the operators' keys to community's authorized_keys and runs the deployment as community: check that this account is meant for the deployment and nothing else.
warning: watchdog: falling back to softdog
  the watchdog will be softdog. It reboots the host when Patroni hangs, but not when the kernel does, and a hung kernel cannot fence itself any other way. A hardware or hypervisor watchdog is better: enable one in the firmware or the VM's settings, and admit again.
warning: watchdog: community's Patroni can reboot this machine
  Patroni arms the watchdog and reboots the whole host when it stops renewing it, which is what makes its failover safe.
